name: GraftSense sensor module kit
one_liner: Plug-and-play sensor modules and controller boards for classrooms and fast prototypes.
intro: GraftSense is a modular hardware kit of sensor modules, expansion boards and learning resources for STEM teaching and rapid prototyping. Modules share a Grove-style connector, so students and engineers can plug sensors into a controller board and get a working demo quickly. The team ships individual modules, 20–30 module kits, course materials and documentation.

tech_stack.value: 300+ sensor, display, motor-driver and expansion modules

tech_stack.label: Controller boards
tech_stack.value: GraftPort expansion boards for Raspberry Pi Pico (RP2040), incl. an Ethernet version

tech_stack.label: Design files
tech_stack.value: Schematic, PCB layout and user docs per module

scope: Custom PCB design for each module
Embedded firmware in MicroPython and Arduino
Sample code, testing and application support
Kit structure planning and supply-chain coordination

name: PottedBaby AI smart planter
one_liner: A planter add-on that senses the soil and lets the plant talk back.
intro: PottedBaby is a compact device that sits in a flower pot, reads soil temperature and moisture, and gives the plant a face and a voice. It shows expressions on a small OLED screen, reacts when someone walks by, and holds spoken AI conversations. It was built as a smart-planter prototype for STEM education, maker projects and interactive desktop products.

tech_stack.value: Soil temperature and moisture sensor (Modbus), PIR motion sensor

tech_stack.label: Audio
tech_stack.value: Microphone and speaker with MAX98357A amplifier

tech_stack.label: Power
tech_stack.value: Rechargeable battery with charge module and power switch

tech_stack.label: Software
tech_stack.value: MicroPython firmware with on-device async scheduling; ASR / LLM / TTS voice dialogue

scope: Embedded firmware: sensor handling, Modbus parsing, AI dialogue workflow

name: Desk AI companion
one_liner: A desk character that shows what your AI coding agent is doing.
intro: A small character-shaped desk device that connects to a computer over Bluetooth and shows the live status of an AI coding agent on its screen, with voice alerts when tasks change. It was built for developers, educators and makers, and comes with swappable 3D-printed accessories such as glasses, ears and hats. A second variant in a white enclosure was also prototyped.

name: PixelSky AI pixel light board
one_liner: An LED pixel board you draw on in a browser, with AI-made animations.
intro: PixelSky is a pixel LED board paired with a browser-based editor. Users draw or generate animations with AI from text or images, preview them live, and push them to the board, which can also show the time and weather. The team built the whole stack: custom LED matrix PCB, ESP32 runtime, web editor and enclosure.

name: ChengXiaoZhi youth maker kits
one_liner: Six small sensor kits in acrylic cases for youth STEAM classes and gifts.
intro: ChengXiaoZhi is a series of six creative electronics kits for youth STEAM education and corporate gifts. Each kit runs on a Raspberry Pi RP2040, pairs a practical sensor with local processing and a display, and comes in a clear acrylic case with 120 minutes of teaching material. Name, logo, PCB silkscreen and packaging can be customized.

name: 24-channel logic analyzer
one_liner: A compact 24-channel, 100 MHz debugging tool for engineers, makers and classrooms.
intro: A pocket-size logic analyzer for debugging digital circuits and embedded projects. It samples 24 channels in real time at up to 100 MHz, accepts 3.3–5 V logic levels, and works with open-source firmware and PulseView software. The team reused a proven open firmware and focused on the hardware, enclosure, packaging and testing so it is ready for batch production.

name: Offline voice-controlled robot dog
one_liner: A small four-legged robot that obeys spoken commands without internet.
intro: A compact four-legged robot that wakes up and follows voice commands offline, with no cloud connection. It walks using several servos, shows expressions on an OLED face and talks back through a built-in speaker. The prototype combines a 3D-printed body, a custom controller board and embedded firmware, aimed at educational robotics kits and STEM demos.
